beur-hagra.1#א: Fish that were cooked or, etc. So wrote Ran and Rambam and Rif, unlike the view of Ribban in name of Rashi who wrote in Tosafot s.v. halachta and brought proof from a cucumber that one cut, etc.; and even though noten taam bar noten taam — according to the second explanation in Rashi who distinguishes that through its sharpness it absorbs from the mouth of boiling fish and this is its absorption, but when they were cooked it is no worse than a cucumber; and Tosafot wrote; however for the first explanation in Rashi, because of the oil on its surface there is no proof. And Semak and Rosh permit when cooked and forbid when roasted, because in cooking there are three noten taam — from the pot to the water and from the water to the vegetable, for most of the taste spreads in water, which is not so in roasting; and proof from what they said one does not smear the oven, etc.; and in Tosafot they rejected this proof too, for an oven cannot be cleaned well and it is visible, and so too here; and this is why he wrote well washed — to exclude a bowl that is not well washed; but stam well washed — for this is the difference between a bowl in which fish came up and a cucumber cut with a knife, as above; and so too that which they permit in chapter 2 of Avodah Zarah boiled oil and hot — learn that stam they rinse them; and Tosafot in Chullin 8b s.v. the slaughterer, etc., and in Avodah Zarah 38b s.v. if, etc.
beur-hagra.1#ב: (Lekut) Noten taam bar noten taam of heter. Specifically of heter — from what he wrote a pot that cooked, etc., in Mordechai. Tosafot Zevachim 96a s.v. and if, etc. (end).
beur-hagra.1#ג: If there is, etc. As above.
beur-hagra.2#א: Even l'chatchila. As he wrote permitted to eat them, etc.
beur-hagra.2#ב: But if, etc. As he wrote in the beginning of Terumot — egg, etc.
beur-hagra.2#ג: And even in the shell. Like an egg of a chick — Chullin 98a; and when it is not peeled he deals with it, as Tosafot wrote there.
beur-hagra.2#ד: And there are, etc. As above.
beur-hagra.2#ה: But to place them, etc. For in this we rely on those who permit. Taz.
beur-hagra.2#ו: And likewise if, etc. This is permitted to all, as above.
beur-hagra.2#ז: And likewise if it was, etc. In such a case, even of prohibition it is permitted, as Tosafot wrote Avodah Zarah 76a s.v. from here, and as he wrote there 38b; and even in a pot it is not forbidden l'chatchila when it is not ben yomo except because of a decree lest it be ben yomo, which is not so here where even ben yomo is permitted by law, as above.
beur-hagra.2#ח: And all this when the food, etc. As he wrote cucumber that one cut, etc., and like the second explanation in Rashi there because of its sharpness; and as he wrote in siman 96 ben yomo or, etc.; and all the more so for Semak who compares to a kortov of halitit in Avodah Zarah 39a that they said even though the master said, etc., end of his words; and therefore he deals with well scraped, for otherwise it is not nat bar lichtmile, as explained above and as Shulchan Aruch wrote there; and some say likewise, etc.
beur-hagra.2#ט: Until there is, etc. See above siman 98 seif 8.
beur-hagra.2#י: Against, etc. See above siman 94 seif 6.
beur-hagra.2#כ: (Lekut) And nevertheless it is not called, etc. From what they said in chapter 6 of Berachot (36b) this hemilta, etc.; and they challenged that although stam their innards are not ben yomo, nevertheless this is a sharp thing; and Semag explained because it is a dry thing and does not spoil for improvement except in a moist thing; and Mordechai explained that they pluck it by hand; and nevertheless it is difficult, behold they cook it in their innards; and Rashi explained that stam their innards are not ben yomo; and Rashi explained that since they cook it in honey it is not sharp because the spice is minimal; and even though Mordechai also explained that they have special vessels for this — Rashba already contradicted this, for if so why did they need to say in hot oil and gentile oil because it is nat bar lichtmile; and see in Mordechai there and in Turei Chayim general rule 61 siman 7; and see above siman 96 seif 2 and 3 and siman 122 seif 6, see there (end).
beur-hagra.3#א: And there are those who forbid, etc. Tosafot there s.v. halachta. And bowls, etc.
beur-hagra.3#ב: And then, etc. For also what is not ben yomo is permitted as noten taam bar noten taam, even for the first taste of Tosafot that there is no prohibition on it since it is not ben yomo — unlike Tosafot there — and Taz.
beur-hagra.3#ג: And the water, etc. For b'dieved does not apply in water, and it is like cooking l'chatchila in cold of prohibition that is not ben yomo, as he wrote at the end of Avodah Zarah; and so too here it absorbed basar b'chalav — and Taz.
beur-hagra.3#ד: But if they were rinsed, etc. For the reasons of Tosafot do not apply here, and it is the actual law of fish that came up, etc., with kutach.
beur-hagra.3#ה: Or in a kli sheni. As he wrote above siman 68.
beur-hagra.3#ו: And if one pours, etc. As he wrote there.
beur-hagra.3#ז: And it forbids, etc. Like the second reason of Tosafot.
beur-hagra.3#ח: But if, etc. That he will do, etc. For as soon as the water cooled on one vessel it becomes a kli sheni — there.
beur-hagra.3#ט: And if it is found, etc. For we do not establish prohibition, as he wrote in the first chapter of Niddah (3b) we say now it fell — Hagahot ShaDa. And further it is a double doubt, etc. — Issur VeHeter and Taz.
beur-hagra.4#_: It appears to me, etc. Taz and Shach who disagreed on this.
beur-hagra.5#_: And nevertheless, etc. As above — we do not establish prohibition — there.
beur-hagra.6#א: Permitted, etc. As he wrote in Avodah Zarah 12a — Rabbah bar Ulla, etc.
beur-hagra.6#ב: And there are those who are stringent, etc. For there it is merely accidental and b'dieved, as Ran wrote, and we do not establish prohibition, as he wrote in seif 5.
beur-hagra.7#א: Salt, etc. For it is like pure salted and impure unsalted. Tosafot Chullin 113a s.v. pure, etc.
beur-hagra.7#ב: And one who is stringent, etc. Tosafot there.
